beats: Hook: in a CNOT the control qubit is never supposed to change (reuse line_qc_cnot_flip_card from QC05-04); feed the target |-> and the control picks up a minus sign. Who is controlling whom? (line_qc_kickback_puppet: the marionette pulls its own string and tips the puppeteer over; reuse line_dog_leash for "who is walking whom".) Same cast as QC07-01: the keeper and the rookie (cast drawing line_qc_revers_fresh_card). Primary source Q24-13: 2025 only names phase kickback (Q25-08 64:12-64:39).

Oracles: a classical function handed over as a box you may only query, never open (Q25-08 55:52-59:11; Q24-13 31:40-35:52): line_qc_kickback_no_peek. The bit oracle |x>|b> -> |x>|b xor f(x)>: the card comes out unchanged and a little lever on the lid flips over when f(x) = 1 (line_qc_kickback_lever_box; code letters the XOR).
Feed it a superposition (Q25-08 59:26-61:14): one call acts on every input at once, but a look returns only one (line_qc_kickback_card_fan; the measurement caveat on screen; QC07-04 picks it up).

The phase oracle |x> -> (-1)^f(x)|x>: the answer goes into a sign instead of a new bit (Q25-08 61:14-63:56; Q24-13 36:09-40:47): line_qc_kickback_sign_box (the card comes back upside down). CZ is the phase oracle for AND (reuse line_qc_rewire_high_five from QC05-05). Tape Q24-13.notes p7.

From bit oracle to phase oracle: set the spare qubit to |-> (Q24-13 41:26-46:55; clip 44:55-45:23, "set b to the minus state and you directly get a phase oracle"): flipping |-> changes only its sign, and that sign can be read as belonging to the input; lettered by code, no drawing.

Phase kickback (Q24-13 47:04-51:29; tape Q24-13.notes p8): look at a CNOT through the X-basis glasses and control and target trade places (reuse line_qc_hbridge_two_glasses from QC05-02, then line_qc_rewire_lead_mover and line_qc_rewire_lead_planner from QC05-05). Her clip 50:22-51:16, "you want to control me, I will secretly give you a phase": back to line_qc_kickback_puppet. Name Cleve, Ekert, Macchiavello and Mosca (1998) only if FACTS.md clears it.

Her other picture (Q24-05 17:06-17:58, clip): if you push someone, you definitely get a force: line_qc_kickback_skaters (both glide apart). Caption it as her analogy for "the control changes too", not as a claim about forces.
Takeaway: a phase oracle plus kickback turns a function into signs, and signs are what interference works on (QC07-04). Skip the questions and the in-class quiz (Q24-13 35:25, 52:28-62:23).

Cover (line_qc_cover_07_03; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the rookie on the bridge of a little puppet theatre, tipped forward because her marionette is pulling its own string; the keeper smiles.
